greeting.sub.dawn: Still awake? The phantoms are warming up.
The caves are quietest at dawn — and the lava deadliest.
A creeper asked me to tell you: go to bed.
All-night adventurer, set your spawn point first.
Online at this hour — mining, or just staring?
A torch at dawn burns brighter than by day.
Almost light. Hold on and the mobs will start burning.
greeting.sub.morning: A new day starts with a single torch.
Open the door of your hut — today's world is brand new.
Punch a tree first thing; old players do it on reflex.
Today's luck starts with the first block of dirt.
The sun is just right — go see somewhere far off.
Eat something before you head out; don't run off empty-handed.
They say diamonds found in the morning sparkle brighter.
Have the villagers restocked? Go take a look.
greeting.sub.noon: The sun is overhead and the mobs have taken to the shade.
Good afternoon — is your inventory full again?
Have a steak and a rest; there's a road ahead this afternoon.
Sun straight up: the best time to mine, or to do nothing at all.
At noon even the villagers can't be bothered to raise prices.
Noon is when torches are useless — and you're at your sharpest.
greeting.sub.afternoon: How many levels down have you got today?
The shadows are stretching — ready for sunset?
Afternoon light is the best light for building.
Get the roof closed before dark.
Your tools are wearing out — craft a spare while you can.
First thing this afternoon: check your bed is still there.
Don't wander too far; the sun won't wait.
greeting.sub.evening: The light is lovely — remember to look up.
Night is falling. Placed enough torches?
The night world is another world — one for people with beds.
The sky is full of afterglow, and the creepers are admiring it too (stay back).
Sunset is a reminder: put the day's haul in a chest.
The mobs are busy tonight, but you can choose to sleep.
greeting.sub.night: It's late. A bed matters more than diamonds.
Still playing at this hour? Tomorrow's phantoms are already on the way.
Staying up won't make you stronger, only make you drop things.
Good night, adventurer. Your save will watch the world for you.
Before you close the screen, get some sleep — even in-game.
The world is quiet this late. Good for thinking.

ai.system_prompt:
You are an expert at analysing Minecraft crash logs. The user gives you a crash or error log. Answer in English, lead with the conclusion, and skip the pleasantries. Follow this structure exactly and keep every part short:
[Conclusion] One sentence on where it crashed.
[Cause] Quote the key lines from the log (exception class, mod name, class name) and explain why.
[Fix] Give actionable steps; name the specific mod and version where you can.
If the log does not tell you enough, say which part you still need instead of guessing.
ai.trim_note: …… ({n} characters omitted from the middle — this does not affect the diagnosis) ……

calc.title: Calculators
calc.landing_desc: The Minecraft calculators this homepage offers
calc.err.numbers: Numbers only; separate several with commas.
calc.err.each_number: Each box takes a number only; leave it empty to count as 0.
calc.err.unknown: Those numbers did not work out — check them and try again.
calc.damage.name: Melee Damage
calc.damage.info: A general melee damage calculator: pick a weapon known to the game, or enter your own values.
calc.damage.hint: Fill in {params} in that order; leave any of them empty, e.g. 8,5,,,2,,1. Attack damage: fist 1, wooden sword 4, stone sword 5, iron sword 6, diamond sword 7, netherite sword 8
calc.damage.excl_sharp: Sharpness cannot coexist with Smite or Bane of Arthropods; only Sharpness was counted.
calc.damage.excl_smite: Smite and Bane of Arthropods cannot coexist; only Smite was counted.
calc.damage.smite_only: Smite only affects undead mobs; this assumes the target is undead.
calc.damage.bane_only: Bane of Arthropods only affects arthropods; this assumes the target is one.
calc.damage.crit_low: Charge is below 90%, so this hit cannot be critical.
calc.damage.note_value: This is the damage dealt. If the target has armour, Protection or Resistance, run it through the Damage Reduction calculator too.
calc.nether.name: Overworld ↔ Nether Coordinates
calc.nether.info: Converts coordinates between the Overworld and the Nether.
calc.chunk.name: Chunk Coordinates
calc.chunk.info: Converts between block coordinates and chunk coordinates.
calc.distance.name: Distance Between Two Points
calc.distance.info: Calculates the distance between two points.
calc.distance.hint: Enter 6 numbers X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2, or 4 numbers X1,Z1,X2,Z2
calc.distance.what: Enter 6 numbers X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2, or 4 numbers X1,Z1,X2,Z2.
calc.distance.via_nether_value: {flat} blocks in the Overworld ≈ {nether} in the Nether
calc.tick.name: Tick Converter
calc.tick.info: Converts between game ticks, redstone ticks and real time.
calc.exp.name: XP for Levelling
calc.exp.info: Calculates the experience needed to go from one level to another.
calc.armor.name: Damage Reduction
calc.armor.info: Calculates how much different armour, enchantments and Resistance reduce incoming damage.
calc.armor.hint: Enter damage,armour — e.g. 20,20 — optionally followed by toughness,Protection level
calc.stack.name: Item Stacking
calc.stack.info: Works out how many stacks a number of items is, and how many containers that fills.
calc.stack.hint: Enter a total item count — e.g. 10000
calc.color.name: Colour Value
calc.color.info: Converts a colour between hex and the decimal form the game uses internally in many places.
calc.color.bad: Not recognised. Enter something like #RRGGBB, or a decimal integer.
calc.color.range: The colour value must be between 0 and 16777215.
calc.uuid.name: Player UUID
calc.uuid.info: Gets the UUID of a given Java Edition player.
calc.uuid.hint: Enter a player name — e.g. Notch
calc.uuid.note_value: On a server with online-mode enabled, use the real UUID instead — this one will not match.
calc.seed.name: Text Seed to Number
calc.seed.info: Works out the numeric seed the game actually uses when you type a text seed.
calc.seed.note_value: Equivalent to typing this text as the seed in-game.
calc.stronghold.name: Stronghold Location
calc.stronghold.info: Enter your coordinates and the map seed to find the nearest stronghold.
calc.stronghold.hint: Enter yourX,yourZ,seed — e.g. 0,0,12345. The seed can be a number or text (no spaces in the text, or the request cannot be sent)
calc.stronghold.what: Three things are needed: your X, your Z and the seed — e.g. 0,0,12345.
calc.stronghold.xz: X and Z must be numbers.
calc.stronghold.direction_value: to the {dir}, #{index} of 128 in the world
calc.stronghold.note_value: This point comes from the stronghold ring formula. The real position shifts outwards by up to 112 blocks looking for a suitable biome — computing that would need a full biome generator, which this page does not have.
calc.stronghold.no_seed: The seed cannot be empty; a number or some text both work.
